Or “because you outdo others in cedar.”
Jehoiakim (“Yahweh raises up”), son of Josiah, reigned 609–598 B.C. (2 Kings 23:34–24:6).
2 Kings 24:6 says only that Jehoiakim “slept with his fathers”; the fulfillment of this oracle is not described.
Abarim, the mountain range east of the Dead Sea, including Mount Nebo.
So the Septuagint and other ancient witnesses; the Hebrew reads “how you will be pitied” or “how favored you will be.”

Coniah, a short form of Jeconiah or Jehoiachin (“Yahweh establishes”), who reigned three months in 598–597 B.C. before being exiled to Babylon (2 Kings 24:8–15). In verses 24–27 the Hebrew shifts between “him” and “you.”
Jehoiachin had sons (1 Chronicles 3:17–18), but none reigned as king.

verses.text: “Woe to the shepherds who ruin and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” declares Yahweh.

Therefore so says Yahweh, God of Israel, about the shepherds who tend my people: “You have dispersed my flock and driven them off, and have not attended to them. Watch: I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds,” declares Yahweh.
“And I will personally round up what is left of my sheep out of every land to which I banished them, and lead them home to their fold, where they will bear young and multiply.
Over them I will set shepherds who will tend them; no longer will they fear or be terrified, and none will be missing,” declares Yahweh.

“Look, days are coming,” declares Yahweh,
“when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch;{a}
he will reign as king and act wisely,
and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.

In his days Judah will be saved,
and Israel will dwell in safety.
And this is the name by which he will be called:
‘Yahweh Is Our Righteousness.’{b}
“Therefore, look, days are coming,” declares Yahweh, “when men will no longer say, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who brought Israel’s sons up from the land of Egypt,’

but, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who brought up and led the offspring of Israel’s house out of the northern land and out of all the lands where I had driven them.’ Then they will dwell on their own soil.”{c}

About the prophets:
Shattered is my heart inside me;
every bone of mine shakes;
I have become like one who is drunk,
like a fellow mastered by wine,
on account of Yahweh,
on account of his holy words.

“For both prophet and priest are godless;
even in my house I have found their wickedness,” declares Yahweh.

“In Samaria’s prophets
I observed something distasteful:
they spoke oracles by Baal
and misled Israel my people.

Yet in Jerusalem’s prophets
I have observed something appalling:
adultery and a life of lies;
they bolster the power of the wicked,
so that none turns back from his wickedness;
to me they are all like Sodom,
and her people like Gomorrah.”

So Yahweh of Armies pronounces this about the prophets:
“I will make them eat wormwood
and drink water laced with poison,
for out of the prophets of Jerusalem
ungodliness has spread over the whole land.”

They keep saying to those who despise me,
‘Yahweh has said, “You shall have peace”’;
and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his heart they say,
‘No calamity will come upon you.’”

For who has stood in the council{f} of Yahweh
to see and to hear his word?
Who has paid attention to his word and listened?

See, Yahweh’s tempest!
Fury is unleashed,
a spinning gale;
on the heads of the wicked it will crash.

The anger of Yahweh will not turn back
until he has executed and accomplished
the intents of his heart.
In the latter days
you will understand it clearly.

“I never dispatched those prophets,
yet off they ran;
I never spoke to them,
yet they uttered prophecy.

But if they had stood in my council,
then they would have proclaimed my words to my people
and turned them from their evil way
and from the evil of their deeds.

“Am I a God near at hand,” declares Yahweh,
“and not a God far off?

Can a man hide himself in secret places
so that I cannot see him?” declares Yahweh.
“Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares Yahweh.
“I have heard what the prophets have said who prophesy falsehood in my name, saying, ‘I have dreamed, I have dreamed!’
How long? Is it in the heart of the prophets who prophesy falsehood, the prophets of the deceit of their own heart—
who plan to make my people forget my name by their dreams that they tell one another, just as their fathers forgot my name for Baal?
The prophet who has a dream—let him recount his dream; but the one who holds my word—let him relate my word with fidelity. What does chaff have to do with grain?” declares Yahweh.
“Is not my word like fire,” declares Yahweh, “and like a hammer that shatters rock?
Therefore, look, I am against the prophets,” declares Yahweh, “who steal my words from one another.
Look, I am against the prophets,” declares Yahweh, “who use their tongues and declare, ‘He declares.’

Mark well, I am against those whose prophecies are false dreams,” declares Yahweh, “who recount them and mislead my people with their falsehoods and their wild boasting, though I never sent or commissioned them; not the slightest benefit do they bring this people,” declares Yahweh.
“Whenever this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, ‘What is Yahweh’s load?’{g} answer them, ‘You are the load, and I will throw you off,’ declares Yahweh.
And the prophet, priest, or commoner who says, ‘Yahweh’s load’—that man and his house I will call to account.
Thus shall you say, each to his neighbor and each to his brother: ‘What has Yahweh answered?’ or ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
But never again bring up ‘Yahweh’s load,’ for each man’s own word becomes his load, and you twist the words of the living God, Yahweh of Armies, our God.
Thus you shall say to the prophet: ‘What has Yahweh answered you?’ or ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
Yet if you persist in saying, ‘Yahweh’s load,’ then here is what Yahweh says: ‘Since you use this phrase, “Yahweh’s load,” though I sent word to you forbidding you to say, “Yahweh’s load,”
for that reason I will indeed lift you up{h} and fling you out of my sight, you along with the city I bestowed on you and your ancestors.
I will lay on you a disgrace that lasts forever, a humiliation without end, never to be forgotten.’”

notes.text: Hebrew tsemaḥ, “sprout, shoot,” a title for the coming king from David’s line (33:15; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12).
Hebrew Yahweh tsidqenu, perhaps a play on the name of King Zedekiah, tsidqiyyahu, “Yahweh is my righteousness.” The Septuagint renders the name as “Josedec” (Brenton), a personal name.
The Septuagint places verses 7–8 after verse 40 (Brenton, printed as 23:40a–b). Verses 7–8 nearly repeat 16:14–15.
Or, with some ancient witnesses, “because of these things.”
Hebrew hevel, “breath, vapor”; they fill you with empty hopes.
Hebrew sod, the council of heavenly beings around Yahweh (compare 1 Kings 22:19–22).

Hebrew massaʾ means both “load, burden” and “oracle, utterance” (literally, something “lifted” by the voice). Verses 33–40 play on the double meaning. “You are the load” follows the Septuagint (“You are the burden,” Brenton) and the Latin Vulgate; the standard Hebrew text reads “What load?” (ʾeth-mah-massaʾ), a difference only in word division.
Hebrew nashithi nasoʾ, “I will utterly forget,” is read by some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient witnesses as nasaʾthi nasoʾ, “I will surely lift up,” continuing the play on massaʾ.

verses.text: Yahweh let me see this: there were two baskets of figs placed in front of Yahweh’s temple. This was after Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile from Jerusalem Jeconiah{a} son of Jehoiakim, Judah’s king, together with Judah’s officials, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers,{b} and had brought them to Babylon.
One basket held very fine figs, like first-ripe figs; the other basket held very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
Then Yahweh asked me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I replied, “Figs—the good ones very good, and the bad ones very bad, too bad to be eaten.”
Then Yahweh’s word came to me:
“So says Yahweh, God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will regard as good the exiles of Judah whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will keep my eyes on them for good and bring them back to this land. I will build them and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know me, that I am Yahweh. They will be my people and I will be their God, for they will return to me with all their heart.

“But like the bad figs, which are too bad to be eaten—so says Yahweh—so will I treat Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the remnant of Jerusalem left in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt.
I will make them a horror, a calamity{c} to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach, a byword, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I drive them.
And I will send among them sword, famine, and plague, until they are wiped out from the soil I gave to them and to their fathers.”

notes.text: Jeconiah, another form of the name Jehoiachin (see the note at 22:24). The deportation took place in 597 B.C. (2 Kings 24:10–16).
Or “the smiths”; the Hebrew masger may mean “locksmith” or “fortifier.”
Hebrew “a horror for calamity.” The Septuagint reads, “I will cause them to be dispersed into all the kingdoms of the earth” (Brenton), and lacks “calamity.”

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah (that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon),{a}
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and all the residents of Jerusalem:

“From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this day—these twenty-three years—Yahweh’s word has come to me, and I have spoken to you, early and persistently, but you have not listened.
And Yahweh sent you all his servants the prophets, early and persistently, but you did not listen or incline your ear to hear,
when they said, ‘Turn now, each of you, from his evil way and his evil deeds, and dwell on the soil that Yahweh gave to you and your fathers from of old and forever.
Do not go after other gods to serve them and bow down to them, and do not provoke me with the work of your hands; then I will do you no harm.’
Yet you did not listen to me, declares Yahweh, so as to provoke me with the work of your hands to your own harm.{b}
“Therefore so says Yahweh of Armies: Because you have not obeyed my words,

mark this, I am summoning every northern clan, declares Yahweh, and Nebuchadrezzar, Babylon’s king, my servant,{c} and I will lead them against this land and those who live in it, and against all the surrounding nations. I will put them under the ban{d} and turn them into an object of dread, of whistling, and of perpetual ruin.
I will silence among them the noise of merriment and the noise of joy, the bridegroom’s voice and the bride’s voice, the grinding of the hand mill and the glow of the lamp.
This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.{e}
Then when seventy years are completed, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, declares Yahweh, for their guilt—the land of the Chaldeans—and make it a desolation forever.
I will bring upon that land all the words I have pronounced against it, everything written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.{f}
For many nations and great kings shall enslave them also, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.”{g}
For this is what Yahweh, Israel’s God, told me: “Accept from my hand this cup brimming with the wine of fury, and give it to every nation I send you to, that they may drink.
They shall drink and stagger and act crazed because of the sword I am sending among them.”
So I took the cup from Yahweh’s hand and made all the nations drink to whom Yahweh sent me:
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, a thing to hiss at, and a curse, as it is this day;
Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, with his attendants, his nobles, and his whole nation;
all the mixed peoples;{h} all the kings of the land of Uz;{i} all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab, and the sons of Ammon;
all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastland across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who clip the corners of their hair;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who dwell in the wilderness;
all the kings of Zimri,{j} all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;
all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another—all the kingdoms of the world that are on the face of the earth. And after them the king of Sheshach{k} shall drink.
“Then say to them, ‘So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Drink, get drunk and vomit, fall and rise no more, because of the sword I am sending among you.’
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, say to them, ‘So says Yahweh of Armies: You must drink!

For, consider: on the very city that bears my name I am starting to bring disaster; and will you go scot-free? Not scot-free will you go, for I am calling down a sword on everyone who lives on the earth, declares Yahweh of Armies.’

“So says Yahweh of Armies:
Look, calamity goes forth
from nation to nation,
and a great storm is stirred up
from the farthest parts of the earth.
And those slain by Yahweh on that day will be from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. They will not be mourned, gathered, or buried; they will be dung on the face of the ground.

Flight will fail the shepherds,
and escape the lords of the flock.

Listen—the cry of the shepherds,
the wail of the lords of the flock!
For Yahweh is ravaging their pasture,

and the peaceful folds are laid waste
because of the fierce anger of Yahweh.

He has quit his thicket like a lion,
for their country has turned into a wasteland
before the sword of the oppressor{m}
and before his burning anger.”

notes.text: That is, 605 B.C., the year of the battle of Carchemish (46:2). The Septuagint lacks the parenthesis (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks most of verse 7, reading only, “But you did not listen to me” (Brenton, modernized).
The Septuagint lacks “and for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, my servant” and reads “a family from the north” (Brenton). In the shorter Greek text, the foe from the north is not named here.
Hebrew ḥerem, the ban of total destruction in holy war.

The seventy years are reckoned in different ways: from 605 B.C. to the fall of Babylon in 539 B.C., or from the destruction of the temple in 586 B.C. to its rebuilding in 516 B.C. (compare 29:10; 2 Chronicles 36:21; Daniel 9:2; Zechariah 1:12). The Septuagint lacks “the king of Babylon” in verse 11 and “the king of Babylon and” in verse 12 (Brenton).

In the Septuagint, verse 13 ends at “written in this book,” and the next words introduce the oracles against the nations, beginning with Elam (Brenton: “The Prophecies of Jeremias against the Nations of Ælam”). These oracles, which stand at chapters 46–51 in the Hebrew, follow at this point in the Greek. See the introductory note.
The Septuagint lacks verse 14 (Brenton). The Greek resumes with verse 15 as chapter 32 in Brenton’s numbering.
Or “all the foreign people”; Hebrew ʿerev, perhaps foreign mercenaries or settlers.
The Septuagint lacks “all the kings of the land of Uz” (Brenton). Uz is a region east or southeast of Israel, the home of Job (Job 1:1).
Zimri is otherwise unknown; it may be a cipher like Sheshach (verse 26), or a corruption. The Septuagint lacks it (Brenton).

Sheshach is a cipher for Babel (Babylon), formed by atbash, a scribal code that replaces each Hebrew letter with its counterpart from the other end of the alphabet (aleph with taw, beth with shin, and so on): b-b-l becomes sh-sh-k. See also 51:41. The Septuagint lacks this sentence (Brenton).
Hebrew uncertain; some read “and I will shatter you.”
So some Hebrew manuscripts (compare 46:16; 50:16); the Septuagint has “the great sword” (Brenton); the standard Hebrew text reads “the oppressor’s fury,” with “fury” repeated in the next line.

verses.text: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah,{a} this word came from Yahweh:

“So says Yahweh: Take your stand in the court of Yahweh’s house and speak to all the towns of Judah that come to bow down in Yahweh’s house all the words I command you to speak to them; hold back not a word.
Perhaps they will listen, and each will turn from his evil way, so that I may relent of the calamity I am planning to bring on them because of their evil deeds.
Say to them, ‘So says Yahweh: If you will not listen to me, to walk in my law that I have set before you,
and to heed the words of my servants the prophets whom I send to you early and persistently, though you have not listened,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and this city I will make a curse for all the nations of the earth.’”
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in Yahweh’s house.
And when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that Yahweh had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him and said, “You must die!

Why have you prophesied in Yahweh’s name, saying, ‘This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be laid waste, without inhabitant’?” And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in Yahweh’s house.
When the officials of Judah heard of these things, they went up from the king’s palace to Yahweh’s house and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of Yahweh’s house.

Then the priests and the prophets spoke to the officials and to all the people: “This man deserves the sentence of death, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears.”
Jeremiah then addressed all the officials and the whole populace: “It was Yahweh who sent me to prophesy against this house and this city every word you have heard.
So now, mend your conduct and your actions, and heed the voice of Yahweh your God; then Yahweh will think better of the disaster he has decreed for you.
As for me, here I am in your hands; do with me whatever seems good and right to you.

Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on its residents, for in truth Yahweh sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing.”
At that the officials and all the populace told the priests and prophets, “No death sentence is due this man, since it is in the name of Yahweh our God that he has addressed us.”
And some of the elders of the land rose up and spoke to the whole assembly of the people:

“Micah of Moresheth{b} prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and said to all the people of Judah, ‘So says Yahweh of Armies:
Zion will be plowed as a field;
Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins,
and the mountain of the house a wooded height.’

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear Yahweh and entreat the favor of Yahweh, and did not Yahweh relent of the calamity he had pronounced against them? But we are about to bring great calamity on ourselves.”
There was also a man who prophesied in Yahweh’s name, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land in words like all those of Jeremiah.
King Jehoiakim, along with all his fighting men and every official, heard what he said, and the king set out to have him killed. Uriah got word of it; in fear he ran off and reached Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt—Elnathan son of Achbor{c} and others with him.
These fetched Uriah back from Egypt and delivered him to King Jehoiakim, who cut him down with a sword and flung his body among the burial plots of the common folk.
Yet Ahikam son of Shaphan{d} stood by Jeremiah and protected him, so that he was not handed over to the mob to be killed.

notes.text: That is, about 609 B.C. This chapter narrates the occasion and outcome of the temple sermon given more fully in 7:1–15.
Micah of Moresheth, the prophet whose book stands among the Twelve; the quotation is Micah 3:12. Micah means “Who is like Yahweh?”
Elnathan (“God has given”) was perhaps the father of Nehushta, Jehoiachin’s mother (2 Kings 24:8). The Septuagint lacks “Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him” (Brenton).
Ahikam son of Shaphan, an official under Josiah (2 Kings 22:12) and father of Gedaliah, later governor of Judah (40:5).

verses.text: At the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah{a} son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
This is what Yahweh told me: “Fashion for yourself thongs and wooden yoke bars, and set them upon your neck.
Then dispatch them{b} to Edom’s king, Moab’s king, the Ammonites’ king, Tyre’s king, and Sidon’s king, through the emissaries who have arrived in Jerusalem to meet Zedekiah, Judah’s king.
Give them a charge for their lords: ‘Thus speaks Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God—tell this to your lords:
It is I who by my great power and my outstretched arm made the earth, with the men and beasts on the face of the earth, and I give it to whomever I see fit.
And now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant; even the beasts of the field I have given him to serve him.
All the nations shall serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time of his own land comes; then many nations and great kings shall make him their servant.{c}

“But any nation or kingdom that will not serve this Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, that nation I will punish with sword, famine, and plague, declares Yahweh, until I have consumed them by his hand.
So pay no heed to your prophets or your diviners, to your dreamers,{d} your fortune-tellers, or your sorcerers, who keep assuring you, “You will never be subject to Babylon’s king.”
A falsehood is what they prophesy to you, and it will only get you removed far from your homeland; I will banish you, and you will be lost.
But the nation that brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave on its own soil, declares Yahweh, to till it and dwell in it.’”
To Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke in the same way: “Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Why must you and your people perish by sword, starvation, and pestilence, as Yahweh has threatened against every nation that refuses to be subject to Babylon’s king?{e}
Do not listen to the words of the prophets who keep telling you, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon,’ for it is a lie they prophesy to you.
I never sent them, declares Yahweh; yet they prophesy lies under my name, and so I will banish you and you will be lost, both you and the prophets prophesying to you.”

Next I addressed the priests and this whole people: “So says Yahweh: Pay no heed to what your prophets prophesy to you, ‘Look, any day now the furnishings of Yahweh’s house will be returned from Babylon,’ for a falsehood is what they prophesy to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city become a ruin?{f}

If they are prophets, and if Yahweh’s word is with them, let them now intercede with Yahweh of Armies, that the vessels left in Yahweh’s house, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.
For Yahweh of Armies has spoken about the columns,{g} the bronze sea, the wheeled bases, and whatever other furnishings remain in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem—
so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, concerning the vessels left in Yahweh’s house, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:{h}
‘To Babylon they shall be carried, and there they shall remain until the day I attend to them, declares Yahweh. Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.’”

notes.text: So a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac (compare verses 3 and 12 and 28:1); the standard Hebrew text reads “Jehoiakim,” probably by copying from 26:1. The Septuagint lacks verse 1 (Brenton). The likely date is 594–593 B.C. (28:1).
Hebrew “send them.” Jeremiah’s symbolic yoke is described in 28:10–11.
The Septuagint lacks verse 7 (Brenton).
Hebrew “your dreams.”
The Septuagint lacks verse 13 (Brenton). Its text of verses 12–22 is markedly shorter throughout.
The Septuagint lacks verse 17 (Brenton).

The two bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, the great bronze basin called “the sea,” and the wheeled stands made for Solomon’s temple (1 Kings 7:15–39). The Septuagint lacks this list, reading only “And as for the remaining vessels” (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks verse 21 and the last sentence of verse 22, ending, “they shall go into Babylon, says the Lord” (Brenton, modernized).

verses.text: In that same year, at the start of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year,{a} in the fifth month (in July–August),{b} the prophet Hananiah{c} son of Azzur, from Gibeon, addressed me in Yahweh’s house before the priests and all the people:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: I have broken the yoke of Babylon’s king.
Within two years’ time I will bring back to this place all the furnishings of Yahweh’s house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed from this place and carried to Babylon.
And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, Judah’s king, along with all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, I will bring back to this place, declares Yahweh, for I will break the yoke of Babylon’s king.”
Then Jeremiah the prophet answered Hananiah the prophet in the presence of the priests and of all the people standing in Yahweh’s house.
Jeremiah the prophet said, “Amen! May Yahweh do so! May Yahweh fulfill the words you have prophesied and bring back from Babylon to this place the furnishings of Yahweh’s house and all the exiles.
Nevertheless, give ear to this word that I am declaring to you and to the whole people listening:
The prophets who came before me and before you from ancient times prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms of war, calamity, and plague.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when that prophet’s word comes to pass, then it will be known that Yahweh truly sent him.”
Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke bar from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

And Hananiah spoke before all the people: “So says Yahweh: Just so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations within two years’ time.” And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.
Some time after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke bar from off the neck of Jeremiah the prophet, Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Go and tell Hananiah, ‘So says Yahweh: Yoke bars of wood you have broken, but in their place you will make{d} yoke bars of iron.

For so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: A yoke of iron I have put on the neck of all these nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they shall serve him; even the beasts of the field I have given him.’”
Jeremiah the prophet then told Hananiah the prophet, “Hear me, Hananiah! Yahweh never sent you, and you have led this people to rely on falsehood.
Therefore so says Yahweh: Look, I am sending you off{e} from the face of the earth. This very year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against Yahweh.”
And Hananiah the prophet died that same year, in the seventh month (in September–October).{f}

notes.text: That is, 594–593 B.C. The Septuagint reads simply “in the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew “the fifth month,” Av.
Hananiah, “Yahweh has been gracious.” The Septuagint calls him “the false prophet” (Brenton), here and elsewhere in the chapter.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “I will make” (Brenton: “but I will make instead of them yokes of iron”).
Hebrew meshallḥakha, a play on the verb “send” (shalaḥ) in verse 15: Yahweh did not send Hananiah as a prophet, but he will send him off the earth.
Hebrew “the seventh month,” Tishri, about two months after the confrontation of verse 1. The Septuagint lacks “that same year” (Brenton).

verses.text: These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders of the exiles, to the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This came after the departure from Jerusalem of King Jeconiah and the king’s mother, the palace officials,{a} the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the artisans, and the smiths.
The letter went by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah dispatched to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. It read:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, to all the exiles whom I have exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and settle in them; plant gardens and eat what they produce.
Take wives and father sons and daughters; take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not dwindle.
And seek the welfare{b} of the city where I have exiled you, and pray to Yahweh on its behalf, for in its welfare will be your welfare.
For so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Do not let the prophets and the diviners among you deceive you, and pay no attention to the dreams you have them dream,{c}
for it is a lie they are prophesying to you in my name. I did not send them, declares Yahweh.
“For so says Yahweh: Only when seventy years for Babylon are completed will I attend to you, and I will fulfill for you my good word, to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I am planning for you, declares Yahweh—plans for peace and not for calamity, to give you a future and a hope.{d}
Then you will cry out to me; you will come and pray to me, and I will hear you.
You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.

Found by you I will be, declares Yahweh; I will turn your captivity around and collect you out of every nation and every place to which I banished you, declares Yahweh, and lead you home to the place from which I sent you into exile.{e}
“Because you have said, ‘Yahweh has raised up prophets for us in Babylon’—
so says Yahweh concerning the king who sits on David’s throne and concerning all the people who dwell in this city, your brothers who did not go out with you into exile:{f}
So says Yahweh of Armies: Look, I am sending among them sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse, a desolation, a thing to hiss at, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
because they did not heed my words, declares Yahweh, which I sent to them by my servants the prophets, early and persistently; and you too would not listen, declares Yahweh.
Hear, then, Yahweh’s word, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon:

So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying a lie to you in my name: Look, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
And because of them this curse will be used by all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon: ‘May Yahweh make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,’{g}
For they committed folly in Israel, sleeping with their neighbors’ wives and speaking in my name falsehoods I never charged them to speak. I know it, and I bear witness, declares Yahweh.”
To Shemaiah the Nehelamite{h} you shall say:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Because you have sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,
‘Yahweh has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be overseer in Yahweh’s house over every madman who prophesies, to put him in the stocks and the collar.
Now then, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is prophesying to you?
For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, “It will be long; build houses and settle in them, and plant gardens and eat what they produce.”’”
Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Send word to all the exiles: ‘So says Yahweh about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Since Shemaiah prophesied to you though I never sent him, and led you to rely on falsehood,

therefore so says Yahweh: Look, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring. He shall have no man dwelling among this people to see the good I will do to my people, declares Yahweh, for he has spoken rebellion against Yahweh.’”

notes.text: Hebrew sarisim, often “eunuchs,” but also a general title for court officials.
Hebrew shalom, “peace, welfare, wholeness,” three times in this verse.
Hebrew “your dreams that you cause to be dreamed”; the Septuagint reads “your dreams which you dream” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew “an end (aḥarith) and a hope,” that is, a hopeful future.
The Septuagint lacks most of verse 14, reading only “And I will appear to you” (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks verses 16–20 (Brenton).
Hebrew qalam, “roasted,” a play on qelalah, “curse,” and on the name Kolaiah (verse 21).
Nehelamite, perhaps “of Nehelam,” an unknown place; it may also suggest ḥalam, “to dream.”

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
“So says Yahweh, God of Israel: Write down in a scroll{a} every word I have spoken to you.

For look, days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will turn back the captivity of my people, Israel and Judah, says Yahweh, and lead them home to the land I gave their fathers, and they will take possession of it.”
These are the words Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

So says Yahweh:
“A cry of panic we have heard,
of dread, and no peace.

Ask now and consider:
can a male give birth?
Why then do I see every man
with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor,
every face turned ashen?

Alas! For that day is great,
with none like it;
a season of distress it is for Jacob,
yet out of it he will be saved.

“On that day, declares Yahweh of Armies,
I will snap the yoke from off your{b} neck,
and your thongs I will tear apart,
and foreigners will no longer make him their slave.

Instead they will serve Yahweh their God
and David their king,
whom I will raise up for them.

Why cry out over your fracture,
your pain past cure?
Because your guilt is great,
because your sins are many,
I have done these things to you.{e}

Therefore all who devour you shall be devoured,
and all your foes, every one, shall go into captivity;
those who plunder you shall become plunder,
and all who prey on you I will give up as prey.

For fresh skin I will grow over you,
and of your wounds I will cure you, declares Yahweh,
since “Castaway” they have named you:
“That is Zion, whom nobody seeks!”

From them will come songs of thanksgiving
and the sound of those who make merry.
I will multiply them, and they will not be few;
I will bring them honor, and they will not be small.

His sons will be as in days of old,
and his congregation will be established before me,
and I will punish all who oppress him.

His prince will be one of his own;
his ruler will come forth from his midst.
I will bring him near, and he will approach me,
for who would dare of himself
to draw near to me? declares Yahweh.

And you will be my people,
and I will be your God.”{g}

Look, the storm of Yahweh!
Fury goes out,
a sweeping tempest;
it will whirl down on the head of the wicked.

The burning anger of Yahweh will not turn back
until he has carried out and accomplished
the purposes of his heart.
In the latter days
you will understand this.{h}

notes.text: Chapters 30–31 are often called “the Book of Consolation.”
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “their neck” (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks verses 10–11 (Brenton); they appear again at 46:27–28, where the Septuagint has them.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
The Septuagint lacks verse 15 (Brenton).
Hebrew tel, a mound of ruins built up from earlier settlements.
The Septuagint lacks verse 22 (Brenton).
Verses 23–24 nearly repeat 23:19–20.

verses.text: “In that time, declares Yahweh, I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they shall be a people to me.”

Again I will build you, and built you shall be,
O virgin Israel!
Again you will take up your tambourines
and go forth in the dance of merrymakers.

Again you will plant vineyards
on Samaria’s hills;
the planters will plant
and enjoy the fruit.

For a day comes when watchmen will call out
on the hill country of Ephraim,
“Up, let us go to Zion,
to Yahweh our God!”’”

Look, I am bringing them from the north country
and gathering them from the far reaches of the earth,
among them the blind and the lame,
the woman with child and the one in labor together;
a great throng, they will return here.

“Hear Yahweh’s word, you nations,
and announce it in the coastlands far away;
say, ‘He who scattered Israel will gather him
and keep him as a shepherd his flock.’

For Yahweh has ransomed Jacob
and redeemed him from a hand too strong for him.

They will come and shout for joy on Zion’s height
and stream toward the goodness of Yahweh—
toward grain, new wine, and oil,
and the young of flock and herd;
their life will be like a well-watered garden,
and they will languish no more.

I will drench the priests’ souls with abundance,
and my people will be filled with my goodness, declares Yahweh.”

So says Yahweh:
“A voice in Ramah is heard,
lamentation, bitter weeping:
Rachel{c} weeping over her children,
refusing to be comforted over her children,
because they are no more.”

So says Yahweh:
“Hold back your voice from weeping
and your eyes from tears,
for there is a reward for your labor, declares Yahweh;
they will return from the land of the enemy.

There is hope for your future, declares Yahweh;
your children will return to their own territory.

“Clearly I have heard Ephraim rocking with grief:
‘You disciplined me, and I took the discipline,
like a calf untrained to the yoke.
Bring me back, that I may come back,
for you are Yahweh my God.

Is Ephraim a dear son to me?
A child of delight?
For as often as I speak against him,
I remember him still.
Therefore my inmost parts yearn for him;
I will surely have compassion on him, declares Yahweh.

How long will you waver,
O faithless daughter?
For Yahweh has created a new thing in the land:
a female surrounds a man.”{d}

So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: “Once more they will use this saying in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes:
‘Yahweh bless you, abode of righteousness,
O holy mountain!’
And Judah and all its cities will dwell in it together, the farmers and those who wander with flocks.
For the exhausted soul I will revive, and each drooping soul I will fill full.”
Upon this I woke and saw; pleasant to me my sleep had been.{e}
“Look, days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.
And as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, to overthrow, to destroy, and to bring harm, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares Yahweh.

In those days they will no longer say,
‘The fathers ate sour grapes,
and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’
Rather, each will die for his own guilt; every man who eats sour grapes, his own teeth shall be set on edge.
“Look, days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will cut a new covenant{f} with the house of Israel and the house of Judah—

unlike the covenant I cut with their ancestors when I took hold of their hand to lead them out from Egypt’s land—that covenant of mine they shattered, even though I was master over them,{g} declares Yahweh.

For this is the covenant I will cut with the house of Israel after those days, declares Yahweh: I will set my law{h} within them, and upon their heart I will write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

And no longer will each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, ‘Know Yahweh,’ for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares Yahweh; for I will forgive their guilt, and their sin I will remember no more.”

So says Yahweh,{i}
giver of the sun to light the daytime,
of the statutes of moon and stars to light the night,
who churns the sea till its breakers thunder—
Yahweh of Armies his name is:

“If this fixed order departs
from before me, declares Yahweh,
then also the offspring of Israel will cease
from being a nation before me for all time.”

So says Yahweh:
“If the heavens above can be measured,
and the foundations of the earth below be searched out,
then I too will reject all the offspring of Israel
for all they have done, declares Yahweh.”
“Look, days are coming,{j} declares Yahweh, when the city will be rebuilt for Yahweh from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
Further still the measuring cord will run, directly to Gareb’s hill, then bend around toward Goah.

The entire vale of carcasses and ashes{k} and every terrace down to the Kidron gorge, as far as the Horse Gate’s corner on the east, shall be holiness to Yahweh. Never again will it be plucked up or thrown down.”

notes.text: The Hebrew of verse 2 is difficult; it may refer to the exodus generation. The Septuagint reads “I found him warm in the wilderness with them that were slain with the sword” (Brenton).
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “to him” (Brenton: “The Lord appeared to him from far”).
Rachel, “ewe.” The wife of Jacob and mother of Joseph and Benjamin, buried near Ramah (compare 1 Samuel 10:2); here she mourns her descendants carried away. Matthew 2:18 cites this verse.

The meaning of “a female surrounds a man” is uncertain and much debated. The Septuagint reads very differently: “for the Lord has created safety for a new plantation: men shall go about in safety” (Brenton). Item for scholarly review.
Perhaps the prophet’s words on waking from a revelatory dream.

Hebrew “cut a covenant,” the idiom for making a covenant, perhaps from the ritual of cutting animals (compare 34:18). The Septuagint reads “make a new covenant” (Brenton). Hebrews 8:8–12 cites verses 31–34 from the Greek.
Hebrew baʿalti, “I was husband (or master)”; the Septuagint reads “and I disregarded them” (Brenton), as in Hebrews 8:9.
Hebrew torah, “instruction, law.”
The Septuagint places verse 37 before verses 35–36 (Brenton 38:35–37).
The written Hebrew text has only “Look, days”; “coming” is supplied by the Hebrew margin (the Qere) and the ancient versions.
Hebrew “valley of the corpses and the fat ashes,” probably the Valley of Ben-hinnom (compare 7:31–32).

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.{a}
At that time the army of Babylon’s king was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the palace of Judah’s king.
For Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him, saying, “Why do you prophesy, ‘So says Yahweh: Look, I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it;
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Chaldeans’ grip but will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king, and will speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye;
to Babylon he will lead Zedekiah, and there he will remain until I attend to him, declares Yahweh; though you fight the Chaldeans, you will not succeed’?”{b}
Jeremiah said, “Yahweh’s word came to me:
‘Look, Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you to say, “Buy for yourself my field in Anathoth, for yours is the right of redemption to buy it.”’

Then Hanamel my cousin came to me, as Yahweh had said, in the court of the guard, and said to me, ‘Buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession and of redemption is yours; buy it for yourself.’ Then I knew that this was Yahweh’s word.
“The Anathoth field I therefore purchased from Hanamel, my uncle’s son, and for it I weighed him out roughly seven ounces{c} of silver.
I signed the deed, sealed it, called in witnesses, and weighed the silver on scales.
Next I took the purchase document—the copy sealed up, holding the stipulations and terms, along with the copy left unsealed—

and handed this document over to Baruch{d} son of Neriah son of Mahseiah while Hanamel my uncle’s son looked on, together with the witnesses whose names were on the document and every Judean seated within the guard’s courtyard.
And before their eyes I charged Baruch:
‘So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: These documents—the sealed bill of sale and the unsealed one—take them and place them inside a clay jar,{e} that they may endure for a long time.
For so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards will yet again be bought in this land.’
“After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to Yahweh:
‘Ah, Lord Yahweh! Look, it is you who made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm; nothing is too wondrous for you.
You show steadfast love to thousands, yet repay the guilt of fathers into the lap of their children after them, O great and mighty God, whose name is Yahweh of Armies,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open to all the ways of mankind, to give each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
Signs and marvels you worked in Egypt’s land, and still today, both in Israel and across humankind, and won for yourself renown, as is plain today.
You brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

Enter they did, and seize it they did, yet to your voice they paid no heed and in your instruction they did not walk; of everything you ordered them to do, not one thing they did. So you have caused all this disaster to meet them.

Look, the siege ramps have reached the city to take it, and because of sword, famine, and plague the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it. What you spoke has come to pass, and look, you see it.
Yet you, Lord Yahweh, have said to me, “Buy the field for silver and call in witnesses,” though the city is given into the Chaldeans’ hand.’”
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Look, I am Yahweh, the God of all flesh. Is anything too wondrous for me?
Therefore so says Yahweh: Look, I am handing this city to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will take it.

The Chaldeans who fight against this city will come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke me.
For from their youth onward Israel’s sons and Judah’s sons have been doing only what is wrong in my eyes; Israel’s sons have only been vexing me with what their hands have made, declares Yahweh.{f}
This city has aroused my anger and my wrath from the day they built it to this day, so that I will remove it from my sight,
on account of every wrong done by Israel’s sons and Judah’s sons to vex me—they and their kings, officials, priests, and prophets, Judah’s men and Jerusalem’s residents alike.
They turned to me the back and not the face; though I taught them early and persistently, they did not listen to accept correction.
They set their detestable things in the house that bears my name, to defile it.

Baal’s shrines they erected in the Ben-hinnom ravine, making sons and daughters of theirs cross through fire for Molech,{g} something I never ordered, which never once came into my thoughts—that they should commit this abhorrent act and so lead Judah into sin.
“Now therefore so says Yahweh, God of Israel, concerning this city of which you say, ‘It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword, famine, and plague’:
Look, I will gather them from all the lands to which I drove them in my anger, my wrath, and great indignation; I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.
They shall be my people, and I will be their God.
One heart and one path I will grant them, so that they revere me always, to their benefit and the benefit of their descendants following them.
An everlasting covenant I will cut with them: never will I turn aside from doing them good, and reverence for me I will place within their hearts, so they do not depart from me.
I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all my heart and all my soul.
For so says Yahweh: Just as I brought all this great calamity on this people, so I will bring on them all the good that I am promising them.
Fields will be bought in this land of which you say, ‘It is a desolation, without man or beast; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.’

Fields will be bought for silver, deeds signed and sealed and witnessed, in the land of Benjamin, in the places around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, of the hill country, of the lowland, and of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes, declares Yahweh.”

notes.text: That is, 588–587 B.C., during the final siege of Jerusalem.
The Septuagint ends the verse “and Zedekiah shall go into Babylon, and dwell there” (Brenton 39:5), lacking the rest.
Hebrew “seventeen shekels,” about 195 grams.

Baruch, “blessed.” Neriah, “Yahweh is my lamp.” Mahseiah, “Yahweh is a refuge.” Baruch was Jeremiah’s scribe and companion (chapters 36, 43, 45). A clay seal impression reading “Berekyahu son of Neriyahu the scribe” has been reported, but its authenticity is disputed. Item for scholarly review.
Hebrew “a vessel of clay,” the kind of jar in which documents were kept.
The Septuagint lacks the second half of verse 30 (Brenton 39:30).
Or “to the king.” Hebrew molekh, a deity or rite of child sacrifice; the Septuagint reads “to king Moloch” (Brenton).

verses.text: A second time Yahweh’s word reached Jeremiah, while he remained shut in within the guard’s courtyard:
“So says Yahweh, who makes it,{a} Yahweh who shapes it to set it firm—Yahweh is his name:
Call to me, and I will answer you and tell you great things, things fenced off,{b} that you have not known.
For so says Yahweh, God of Israel, about the houses of this city and the houses of Judah’s kings that are pulled down to make a defense against the siege ramps and the sword:
They come to fight the Chaldeans and to fill them{c} with the corpses of men whom I struck down in my anger and fury, for I have hidden my face from this city because of all their wickedness.
Look, I will bring to it new flesh and healing; I will heal them and uncover for them a wealth of peace and faithfulness.
I will turn back the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel and build them up as at the first.
I will purify them from all the guilt by which they sinned against me, and pardon all the guilt by which they sinned and rebelled against me.

And this city shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and a glory before all the nations of the earth who hear of all the good I do for them; they will tremble and quake over all the good and all the peace I provide for it.

“So says Yahweh: Yet again there will sound out in this place—of which you keep saying, ‘Wasteland, bare of human and animal’—in Judah’s towns and along Jerusalem’s deserted lanes, void of human, of resident, of animal—

the sound of gladness and the sound of joy, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, the voice of those who say,
‘Give thanks to Yahweh of Armies,
for Yahweh is good,
for his steadfast love endures forever!’
as they bring thank offerings into Yahweh’s house. For I will turn back the captivity of the land as at the first, says Yahweh.
“So says Yahweh of Armies: In this place that is waste, without man or beast, and in all its towns, there will again be pasture for shepherds resting their flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, of the lowland, and of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in Judah’s towns, flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, says Yahweh.
“Look, days are coming, declares Yahweh,{d} when I will fulfill the good word I spoke to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will make sprout for David a righteous Branch,{e} and he will execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will dwell securely, and this is what she will be called: ‘Yahweh Our Righteousness.’{f}
For so says Yahweh: David shall never lack a man sitting on the throne of the house of Israel,
nor shall the Levite priests ever be short of a man in my presence, presenting whole burnt offerings, sending up grain offerings in smoke, and preparing sacrifices every day.”
Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“So says Yahweh: Were you able to annul my covenant of the daytime and my covenant of the night, so that daytime and night no longer arrive in their season,
then also my covenant with David my servant may be broken, so that he has no son to reign on his throne, and my covenant with the Levitical priests my ministers.
As the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me.”
Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Have you not observed what this people have said: ‘The two clans{g} that Yahweh chose, he has rejected them’? So they despise my people, as though they were no longer a nation in their sight.
So says Yahweh: Unless I fixed my covenant of daytime and night, and appointed the statutes governing heaven and earth,

then I will also reject the offspring of Jacob and David my servant, and will not choose from his offspring rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will turn back their captivity and have compassion on them.”

notes.text: So the Hebrew, “who makes it” (that is, who brings his plan to pass). The Septuagint reads “who made the earth and formed it” (Brenton).
Hebrew betsuroth, “fortified, inaccessible”; some Hebrew manuscripts read netsuroth, “hidden.”
Hebrew “them,” probably the houses. The text of verses 4–5 is difficult.
Verses 14–26 are absent from the Septuagint (Brenton). They expand the promise of 23:5–6 and are among the longest passages in the Hebrew text with no Greek counterpart. Item for scholarly review.
Compare 23:5, where the same promise appears in slightly different words.
Hebrew Yahweh Tsidqenu. At 23:6 the name is given to the king; here it is given to the city.
Probably Israel and Judah, though some take it as Judah and the house of David, or the royal and priestly lines of verses 17–22.

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, with his whole army, every kingdom of the earth under his rule, and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem and against all its towns:
“So says Yahweh, God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah; tell him, ‘So says Yahweh: Look, I am delivering this city into the grip of Babylon’s king, and he will burn it with fire.

And you yourself will not slip from his grip; you will surely be seized and handed over to him. Your eyes will look into the eyes of Babylon’s king, his mouth will speak to your mouth, and to Babylon you will go.
Yet hear Yahweh’s word, O Zedekiah king of Judah: So says Yahweh concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

In peace you will die. And as spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn spices for you and lament for you, “Alas, lord!” For I myself have spoken the word, declares Yahweh.’”
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

while the army of Babylon’s king was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the towns of Judah still holding out, Lachish and Azekah;{a} for these alone among Judah’s towns remained as fortified cities.
The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim release{b} to them:
that each should set free his Hebrew slave, male or female, so that no one should hold a fellow Judean in bondage.
And all the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed: each would set free his male and female slave and no longer hold them in bondage. They obeyed and let them go.
Later, though, they reversed course, fetched back the menservants and maidservants they had freed, and subdued them again into servitude.{c}
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
“So says Yahweh, God of Israel: I myself cut a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves, saying,

‘When seven years end{d} you shall each release your Hebrew kinsman who was sold to you; six years he serves you, and then you must dismiss him from you a free man.’ Your ancestors, though, paid me no heed and turned no ear.
You yourselves turned back today and did what was right in my eyes, proclaiming release each to his neighbor, and you cut a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.
But then you turned and profaned my name: each took back his male and female slave whom you had sent away free at their own desire, and you forced them to be your male and female slaves.

Therefore so says Yahweh: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming release each to his brother and to his neighbor. Look, I proclaim to you a release, declares Yahweh—to the sword, to plague, and to famine;{e} and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
The men who overstepped my covenant, not upholding the covenant’s words that they cut in my presence, I will render like{f} the calf they sliced in two, between whose halves they walked—
the officials of Judah, the officials of Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf.
I will give them into the hand of their enemies and of those who seek their life; their corpses shall be food for the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth.
And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will give into the hand of their enemies, of those who seek their life, of the army of Babylon’s king that has withdrawn from you.{g}

Look, I am giving command, declares Yahweh, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, take it, and burn it with fire; and the towns of Judah I will make a desolation without inhabitant.”

notes.text: Lachish and Azekah were fortress towns in the Judean lowland southwest of Jerusalem. Ostraca found at Lachish (the “Lachish letters”) are reported to mention watching for the signals of Azekah, probably from this period.
Hebrew deror, “release, liberty,” the term used for the Jubilee in Leviticus 25:10.
The Septuagint shortens verses 10–11 (Brenton 41:10–11).
So the Hebrew, counting inclusively (compare Deuteronomy 15:1, 12). The Septuagint reads “When six years are accomplished” (Brenton).
The Hebrew plays on deror, “release”: those who would not release their slaves are released to disaster.
Hebrew lacks “like”; the comparison is implied. The rite of passing between the halves of an animal (compare Genesis 15:9–17) called down its fate on any party who broke the covenant.
The Babylonian army had temporarily lifted the siege when an Egyptian force approached (37:5).

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
“Go to the house of the Rechabites,{a} speak with them, and bring them into Yahweh’s house, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.”
So I took Jaazaniah{b} son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, with his brothers and all his sons and the whole house of the Rechabites,

and I brought them into Yahweh’s house, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was beside the officials’ chamber, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, keeper of the threshold.
Then I set before the men of the Rechabite house bowls brimming with wine, and cups, and said to them, “Drink wine.”
But they answered, “We drink no wine, for Jonadab{c} son of Rechab, our father, commanded us: ‘You shall drink no wine, neither you nor your sons, for all time.

No house shall you build, no seed shall you sow, no vineyard shall you plant or own; but in tents you shall dwell all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the land where you sojourn.’
We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, in all he charged us: to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters,
and to build no houses to dwell in. Vineyard, field, and seed we have none.
We have lived in tents, and have obeyed and done all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
But when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, ‘Come, let us go into Jerusalem before the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram.’ So we are living in Jerusalem.”
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will you not take correction and listen to my words? declares Yahweh.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, have been kept; to this day they drink none, for they obey their father’s command. But I have spoken to you early and persistently, and you have not listened to me.

Every one of my servants the prophets I dispatched to you, rising early to send them, with the message: ‘Come back, each of you, from your wicked course; make your conduct good; stop chasing other gods to worship them; then you will remain on the soil I granted you and your ancestors.’ Yet you lent no ear and heeded me not.
The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their father gave them, but this people has not listened to me.

Therefore so says Yahweh, God of Armies, God of Israel: Look, I am bringing on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the calamity I have pronounced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, I called to them and they did not answer.”

But to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said, “So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father, kept all his commands, and done all he commanded you,
therefore so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Jonadab son of Rechab shall never lack a man to stand before me for all time.”{d}

notes.text: The Rechabites were a clan descended from Jonadab son of Rechab (verse 6), who kept a semi-nomadic life of abstinence; they are linked with the Kenites in 1 Chronicles 2:55. Rechab may mean “rider” or “charioteer.” The Septuagint calls them “the Archabin” (Brenton).
Jaazaniah, “Yahweh listens.” The Septuagint calls him “Jechonias the son of Jeremin” (Brenton).
Jonadab (also Jehonadab), “Yahweh is generous.” He took part in Jehu’s purge of Baal worship (2 Kings 10:15–23), about 840 B.C., some two and a half centuries before this episode.
To “stand before” Yahweh is the language of service. The Septuagint adds “before my face while the earth remains” (Brenton).

verses.text: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah,{a} this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:

“Take for yourself a scroll{b} and write on it every word I have spoken to you against Israel and against Judah and against all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, in the days of Josiah, until this day.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear of all the calamity I intend to do to them, so that each will turn from his evil way, and I may forgive their guilt and their sin.”
Jeremiah therefore summoned Baruch son of Neriah, and from Jeremiah’s lips{c} Baruch inscribed on a scroll every word that Yahweh had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah charged Baruch: “I am restricted;{d} I cannot enter Yahweh’s house.

So you go, and on a fast day read from the scroll you wrote at my dictation the words of Yahweh in the hearing of the people in Yahweh’s house; read them also in the hearing of all Judah who come in from their towns.
Perhaps their plea will fall before Yahweh, and each will turn from his evil way; for great is the anger and the wrath that Yahweh has pronounced against this people.”
And Baruch son of Neriah did all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the book the words of Yahweh in Yahweh’s house.

In the fifth year{e} of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month (in November–December),{f} all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the towns of Judah to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before Yahweh.

Then Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah in Yahweh’s house, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of Yahweh’s house, in the hearing of all the people.
Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan, on hearing out of the book every one of Yahweh’s words,

down he went to the palace, into the secretary’s room. Seated there were the officials, all of them—Elishama the secretary; Delaiah, Shemaiah’s son; Elnathan, Achbor’s son; Gemariah, Shaphan’s son; Zedekiah, Hananiah’s son; and every other official.
And Micaiah told them all the words he had heard when Baruch read the book in the hearing of the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch, saying, “The scroll that you read in the hearing of the people—take it in your hand and come.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
They said to him, “Sit down and read it in our hearing.” So Baruch read it in their hearing.
When they heard all the words, they turned in alarm to one another and said to Baruch, “We must certainly report all these words to the king.”
Baruch they then questioned: “Explain to us—these words, how did you come to write them all? Was it from his lips?”
Baruch answered them, “From his own mouth he recited all these words to me, while I wrote them in ink on the scroll.”
Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go, hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.”
So they went in to the king in the court, having deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and reported all the words in the king’s hearing.
Then the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe. Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and of all the officials standing beside the king.
The king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month (in November–December),{g} with a fire burning in the brazier before him.
Each time Jehudi had read out three or four columns,{h} the king sliced them away with a penknife and tossed them onto the brazier’s flames, till the scroll was burned up whole on the brazier fire.
Neither king nor courtier, though hearing all these words, felt any dread; no one ripped his clothes.
Even when Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.{i}
And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But Yahweh hid them.
Now after the king had burned the scroll with the words Baruch wrote at Jeremiah’s dictation, Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Take again another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, ‘So says Yahweh: You have burned this scroll, saying, “Why have you written on it that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and cut off from it man and beast?”
Therefore so says Yahweh concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night.

I will punish him and his offspring and his servants for their guilt; I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah all the calamity I pronounced against them, but they would not listen.’”

Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, who wrote on it at Jeremiah’s dictation all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.

notes.text: That is, 605–604 B.C., the year of the battle of Carchemish (46:2).
Hebrew “a scroll of a book,” a roll of papyrus or leather.
Hebrew “from the mouth of Jeremiah”; so also “at my (his) dictation” in verses 6, 17, 27, 32.
Hebrew ʿatsur, “restrained, hindered”; the reason is not stated. The Septuagint reads “I am in prison” (Brenton), though 36:19, 26 suggest he was not under arrest.
That is, 604–603 B.C. The Septuagint reads “in the eighth year” (Brenton).
Hebrew “the ninth month,” Kislev. A fast may have been called because of the Babylonian advance; 604 B.C. saw Nebuchadnezzar’s campaign against Ashkelon.
Hebrew “the ninth month,” Kislev, the cold, rainy season.
Hebrew delathoth, “doors,” that is, columns of writing on the scroll.
The Septuagint reverses the sense: “But Elnathan and Godolias suggested to the king that he should burn the roll” (Brenton).

verses.text: Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, having been made king over the land of Judah by Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of Yahweh that he spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal{a} son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet with this request: “Pray on our behalf to Yahweh our God.”
Jeremiah at that point still moved freely in and out among the populace; nobody had yet locked him up.
Meanwhile Pharaoh’s army had come out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the report of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.{b}
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah the prophet:

“So says Yahweh, God of Israel: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah who sent you to me to inquire of me: Look, Pharaoh’s army, which came out to help you, is about to return to its own land, to Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will come back and fight against this city; they will capture it and burn it with fire.
So says Yahweh: Do not fool your own souls by telling yourselves, ‘Off from us the Chaldeans are sure to march.’ Depart they will not.

Even if you were to strike down the whole army of the Chaldeans fighting against you, and there remained among them only wounded men, each in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.”
Now when, on account of Pharaoh’s forces, the Chaldean host had pulled back from Jerusalem,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to take his share{c} there among the people.

But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, a captain of the guard was there named Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
“False!” Jeremiah replied. “To the Chaldeans I am not defecting.” Irijah, though, refused to hear him; he laid hold of Jeremiah and led him off to the officials.
The officials were enraged at Jeremiah; they beat him and put him in confinement in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into a prison.
So Jeremiah went into the cistern house,{d} into the vaulted cells, and remained there many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent and had him brought, and the king questioned him secretly in his house: “Is there any word from Yahweh?” Jeremiah said, “There is.” And he said, “Into the hand of Babylon’s king you will be given.”
Jeremiah further asked King Zedekiah, “In what have I sinned against you, your courtiers, or this people, that you have locked me up in a jail?
Where now are your prophets who prophesied to you, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land’?
So now, my lord king, kindly hear me: may my petition come before your face. Do not return me to Jonathan the secretary’s house, or there I shall perish.”

King Zedekiah then gave the order. Jeremiah was entrusted to the guard’s courtyard, and each day a round loaf from the Street of the Bakers was handed him, till the city’s bread ran out entirely. Thus Jeremiah stayed on in the guard’s courtyard.

notes.text: Jehucal, “Yahweh is able.” He is called Jucal at 38:1. A clay seal impression reading “Yehukal son of Shelemyahu” has been reported from excavations in Jerusalem. Item for scholarly review.
This lifting of the siege is the setting of 34:21–22 as well.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; perhaps to receive a share of a family inheritance (compare 32:6–15). The Septuagint reads “to buy thence a property in the midst of the people” (Brenton).
Hebrew “the house of the cistern,” an underground dungeon.

verses.text: Word of what Jeremiah was proclaiming to the whole populace reached the ears of Shephatiah, Mattan’s son; of Gedaliah, Pashhur’s son; of Jucal, Shelemiah’s son; and of Pashhur, Malchiah’s son:
“So says Yahweh: Whoever remains in this city will die by sword, by famine, and by plague; but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; he will have his life as a prize of war{a} and live.
So says Yahweh: This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of Babylon’s king, and he will capture it.”

The officials then told the king, “This fellow must be executed. He is slackening the hands of the fighting men still left in the city, and of all the people too, with words like these. This fellow seeks not the good of this people but its ruin.”
“There—he is in your power,” King Zedekiah replied, “for against you the king is helpless.”

Jeremiah they took and flung into Malchiah the king’s son’s cistern within the guard’s courtyard, lowering him on cords. Water there was none in the pit, only sludge, and down into the sludge Jeremiah sank.
Ebed-melech{b} the Cushite, a court official in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate.
Ebed-melech went out from the king’s house and spoke to the king:
“My lord the king, these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, casting him into the cistern; he will die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city.”
Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, “Take thirty men{c} with you from here and draw Jeremiah the prophet up out of the cistern before he dies.”

So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went into the king’s house, to a place beneath the storehouse, and took from there worn-out rags and old clothes, and let them down by ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, “Put the worn-out rags and clothes under your armpits, beneath the ropes.” Jeremiah did so.
Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and drew him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
King Zedekiah summoned Jeremiah the prophet, bringing him to himself at the third entryway of Yahweh’s house. “A question I shall put to you,” the king told Jeremiah. “Keep nothing back from me.”
Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me.”
Then King Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah, “As Yahweh lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death or give you into the hand of these men who seek your life.”

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “So says Yahweh, God of Armies, God of Israel: If you will indeed go out to the officers of Babylon’s king, your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned with fire; you and your household will live.
But if you do not go out to the officers of Babylon’s king, this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans; they will burn it with fire, and you yourself will not escape from their hand.”
“It is the Judeans gone over to the Chaldeans that I dread,” King Zedekiah told Jeremiah, “that I may be surrendered into their hands and they make sport of me.”
Jeremiah said, “You will not be handed over. Obey, I beg you, the voice of Yahweh in what I am telling you, and it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to go out, this is what Yahweh has shown me:

Look, all the women left in the house of Judah’s king will be led out to the officers of Babylon’s king, and they will say,
‘They misled you and overcame you,
those trusted friends of yours;{d}
now that your feet are sunk in the mire,
they have turned away from you.’

Every wife and son of yours will be marched out to the Chaldeans. Neither shall you escape their grip; in the grip of Babylon’s king you will be caught, and this city will be burned{e} to the ground.”
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “Let no one know of these words, and you will not die.
Should the officials learn that I have talked with you, and come and demand, ‘Disclose to us what you told the king and what the king told you; conceal nothing from us and we will spare your life,’
then you shall say to them, ‘I was presenting my plea before the king, that he would not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.’”

Sure enough, the officials all came to Jeremiah and interrogated him, and he gave them answer exactly in the terms the king had ordered. Then they left off questioning him, since nobody had overheard the matter.
And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.{f}

notes.text: Hebrew “his life shall be to him as spoil,” that is, he will escape with his life and nothing more.
Ebed-melech, “servant of the king.” A Cushite, that is, from the upper Nile region (Nubia). He is promised deliverance in 39:15–18.
So the Hebrew, followed by the Septuagint (Brenton). One Hebrew manuscript is reported to read “three men,” which some prefer as more likely for the task.
Hebrew “the men of your peace.” The lines echo Obadiah 7.
So the ancient versions; the Hebrew reads “and you will burn this city,” that is, you will be the cause of its burning.
The last clause of the Hebrew, “and it came to pass when Jerusalem was taken,” introduces 39:1 in many translations.

verses.text: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month (in December–January),{a} Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and his whole army came against Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
In Zedekiah’s eleventh year, in the fourth month (in June–July),{b} on the ninth day of the month, the city wall was breached.

Then all the officials of Babylon’s king came in and took their seats in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag,{c} and all the rest of the officials of Babylon’s king.

On seeing them,{d} Zedekiah king of Judah and every fighting man took flight; under cover of night they slipped out of the city along the royal garden path, by the gateway between the double walls, and he headed off in the direction of the Arabah.
